key_insight: Looped reasoning models implement iterative, attractor-like latent dynamics that perform stepwise refinement of intermediate answers, producing more stable and reusable computational subroutines than equivalent feedforward models.
problem_solved: Provides a mechanistic explanation for why looping layers in the latent dimension improves reasoning: it changes internal trajectories and circuit reuse, not just parameter count or depth.
method: Compare looped vs. feedforward models on reasoning tasks using trajectory analysis (PCA/UMAP) to visualize latent dynamics over iteration steps.
Use representational similarity (CKA), linear probes and ablations to identify where and how information accumulates, and to locate reusable subcircuits.
Examine attention/gating patterns and perform causal interventions (weight/activation ablations) to link dynamics to performance changes.
impact: Clarifies how iterative latent looping modifies computation, enabling practitioners to design and debug models that better perform multi-step reasoning, and to trade off depth, compute and interpretability more effectively.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: feedforward stack vs. looped stack (single layer reused across iterations).
Latent trajectory plot (PCA/UMAP) showing iterative refinement converging to an attractor for looped models vs. transient paths for feedforward models.
Heatmaps of attention/gating and a small circuit diagram highlighting reusable submodules discovered by probes/ablations.
Bar chart of ablation experiments showing performance drop when disrupting identified circuits in looped vs. feedforward models.
paper_title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models
paper_authors: Hugh Blayney, Álvaro Arroyo, Johan Obando-Ceron, Pablo Samuel Castro, Aaron Courville
